correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the edge ideal from three simple even cycles and bipartite incidence rank, derived the orbit-support codimension z+(|U|-1)(|V|-1)-2, enumerated all support rectangles with z<=5 to rule out missing codimension<3 singular strata, then computed differential-span criteria for all six support types. The three irreducible codimension-three families have the stated free coordinate choices, and each generic local elimination yields the quadratic ordinary node. A separately replayed exact-integer finite checker confirmed 6,793 compatible strata across ten parameter triples, which is corroboration rather than an infinite proof. Higher-codimension strata remain unclassified.

value.rationale: The theta family is the first natural non-complete-intersection (three cycle binomials, height two) bipartite edge-toric test family beyond one-cycle hypersurfaces. Complete classification of its maximal-dimensional singular strata, exact closed multivariate component count, and generic threefold node models give geometrically usable information about the exceptional/crepant behavior of possible resolutions. This is not a routine numeric substitution or a restatement of ideal generators; the three families require global Jacobian support analysis.
